SK2112 The local is declared nullable and is never null

A local is declared T?, is assigned once with a value the compiler proves non-null, and is never assigned again.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

The reverse direction of the nullable migration. A ? the flow analysis proves unnecessary is a null check every subsequent line has to justify for nothing, and it trains the reader to stop believing the annotations — which is the whole value of having them. The declaration is the one place the claim can be corrected, and for a local it can be corrected without asking anybody, because nothing outside the method can see it.

Example

Instead of:

string? name = user.DisplayName ?? "anonymous";
return name.Length;

Write:

string name = user.DisplayName ?? "anonymous";
return name.Length;

When it does not fire

⚠ Locals only, and the two halves of `ReturnTypeCanBeNotNullable` are cut with a reason. Narrowing a method's return annotation propagates to every call site through var: var x = M(); infers string? today and string afterwards, so a later x = null becomes a new warning in a file the analyzer never saw. A DiagnosticAnalyzer is handed one syntax tree and cannot enumerate callers, so the rule would be right about the method and wrong about the program. ReSharper does it from a solution-wide index; Skala has no such index at analysis time and says so rather than guessing. The same cascade inside one method is guarded directly: a local used to initialise a var declaration is declined. ⚠ Reference types only. int? i = 1; is not the same edit at all — removing that ? changes the type, not an annotation, and breaks HasValue, boxing and comparison to null. ⚠ A single assignment. The initialiser must exist and its flow state must be NotNull, and no other assignment to the local may appear anywhere in the enclosing member, lambdas and local functions included; ref and out uses are declined because the callee decides the value. ⚠ The rule withdraws where nullable annotations are disabled at the declaration. There the flow state of every expression is NullableFlowState.None, which is not NotNull — the ? is already CS8632 and removing it is the compiler's finding, not this one. A rule that read NullableAnnotation instead of the flow state would report nothing at all in either context, because GetTypeInfo on a written TypeSyntax returns NullableAnnotation.None for string and string? alike.
